title: Serena Williams Is Back! How to Watch Wimbledon for Free
summary:
Tennis fans, get ready! The world’s most famous tennis tournament, Wimbledon, starts on Monday, June 29. And guess what? Serena Williams is back! She hasn’t played in a Grand Slam since 2022, but now she’s returning as a wild card—that means she got a special invite even though she’s not ranked. She even won Wimbledon back in 2016.

Wimbledon happens in London, England, on grass courts. The matches start super early for us in the U.S.—6 a.m. Eastern Time! But don’t worry, you can watch on ESPN, ESPN2, or ABC. If you don’t have cable, you can still stream it live online for free. How? By using free trials from services like DirecTV, Hulu + Live TV, or Fubo. They all offer five-day free trials, so you can sign up, watch the matches, and cancel before you pay anything.

Serena might play her first match on Monday or Tuesday. And here’s a cool bonus: she and her sister Venus are also playing doubles together! That starts on Thursday, July 2. Plus, keep an eye out for celebrities in the crowd—Taylor Swift, Harry Styles, and even Prince William and Kate Middleton have been spotted at Wimbledon before.

So grab some strawberries and cream (a Wimbledon tradition!) and tune in. It’s going to be a smashing good time!
why_it_matters: Watching a great athlete like Serena make a comeback can inspire you to try a new sport or keep working hard at something you love.

background_read: Wimbledon, which began in 1877, is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and is famous for its grass courts and the rule that players must wear white.
Serena Williams (one of the greatest women's tennis players, with 23 Grand Slam singles titles) hasn't been in a major tournament for a while, so her return is big news.
She and her sister Venus Williams (also a tennis superstar) have won many doubles championships together.
Article_Structure: WHO: Serena Williams, her sister Venus, and celebrities like Taylor Swift and Prince William.
WHAT: Serena returns to Wimbledon as a wild card, with free ways to watch on TV and online.
WHERE: At the Wimbledon tennis tournament in London, England, on grass courts.
WHY: Because she got a special invite and fans can follow her comeback, plus enjoy a famous tennis tradition.

perspectives.description: Fans are excited to see one of the best players ever back on the court. Her comeback shows that you can take a break and still return stronger.
Some people feel that giving a wild card to a famous player can be unfair to other players who earned their ranking by competing all year.
Wimbledon is more than just sports: its traditions like strawberries and cream, and the chance to spot celebrities, make it a special summer event that many people enjoy following together.
